newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wants reliable grain buyers - USDA's Rominger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wants reliable grain buyers - USDA's Rominger.

text.p: The United States proved it was a reliable grain supplier during 1996's market jitters and wants its customers to return the favor, Deputy Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger said Monday.

"We kept our markets open. We mean it when we say the United Sttes will remain a reliable supplier to the world," Rominger said in remarks delivered by satellite to a U.S. Feed Grains Council conference on enhanced value grain.
He immediately followed by saying the United States would like to see reliable buyers.
Grain prices soared last year because of tight supplies worldwide. With the fall harvest, stockpiles are fatter and there is more competition for export sales.

Also during the satellite connection, Gus Schumacher, head of the Foreign Agriculture Service, said the Agriculture Department would fight for full-funding of the Market Access Program despite claims it was part of "corporate welfare."
